source_reasoning: The five observation sites drain the correct context-owned native scope before returning their candidate or recording success. Cached dispatch drops the native pass, resolves the original body result against observation and increments its count only after both succeed. The resolver retains the earlier body error as source and simultaneous typed secondary observation. CompiledLayout observes native layout/pipeline creation before publication. FastPath prepares and packs before its scope, then observes bind-group creation and writes before returning Prepared.

UniformArena publishes a new chunk and resets its used cursor only after successful observation. Already-consumed existing slots and encoded commands are not rolled back after later failure. Copy checks both typed logical ends, retains zero-extent native admission and does not increment the dispatch count. Actual Device-axis admission precedes preparation and writes. Borrowed/browser policy gains no blocking wait. after_submit callbacks run in registration order only after context.submit returns Ok; this is not GPU completion.

Transient Progress retains actual poll and optional native causes, is not published as a successful Kernel or native pipeline cache admission, and removes an older same-entry DeviceHandled entry. Native-only rejection caching is unchanged. Progress creates no new Compiled transition; a previous Compiled marker may remain, with compiled() re-entering absent cache admission before returning a handle. Native-only conversions retain ordinary direct native identity. No recovery of prior device-handled errors is claimed.

The F05/F23 ledger explicitly accepts provided-variant whole-block skip behavior. A used 16-byte vec4 block supplied a 64-byte Mat4 skips that write and may successfully remain zero, in both baseline and current packers. Earlier overlapping writes remain intact. This is settled preservation, not a pending repair or fast/static mismatch. Missing/unsupported fast variants still fail; static inner Mat3 ranges can fail after their outer span fits. Fast offsets remain bounded by sealed Naga metadata and the 256-byte fast cap. Broad prose must not imply all oversized supported writes fail.

Peer provenance has three byte-exact files and four source-equivalent formatting differences: cfg import order, one signature wrap, one closure wrap and a trailing newline. Both peer and committed Root hashes are recorded. All seven committed files are not described as byte-exact peer source.
